name: Farmer
description: Though not educated, <name> was wise. [He/She] knew when to plant to avoid a frost, and could coax oxen to plough a perfect furrow. Life was hard but Nature was bountiful. <name> had much to be thankful for.

name: Swineherd
description: Wandering the forest with rooting hogs for company, carrying a stout stick for beating down acorns and interlopers...this was all <name> knew. Whiling away the hours, chewing mushrooms, alone with [his/her] imagination. Other people's jobs were more onerous, <name> believed.

name: Marshal
description: A wanderer from Barcelona, <name> had the gift of healing animals, and occasionally humans at a pinch. [He/She] was learned, understanding the Moorish faith, and the teachings of Galen and Aristotle. <name> had an excellent sense of humour!

name: Cottar
description: With a field to plough and a cottage to live in, <name> laboured hard. [He/She] had mainly worried about death and taxes. With a dozen destitute dependents, <name> had feared paying out all [his/her] livestock in heriots to the Lord if any died.

name: Gardener
description: <name> had found peace within the wattle fences of the garden, filled with scented flowers and herbs. [He/She] knew their properties well, as food and medicine. Time stood still under the trellises, and <name> would bathe in the scent of new growth.

name: Reeve
description: Rising from humble serf to Reeve offered <name> a coveted place at [his/her] lord's table. Yet overseeing [his/her] fellow labourers was a thankless task. With so much to manage, why not take a little for oneself? <name> certainly felt justified.

name: Herbalist
description: Having once seen a copy of De Materia Medica at Oxford, <name> became a lifelong devotee Dioscorides. Blending this with the teachings of [his/her] mentor, an elderly nun and plantswoman, <name> felt confident in pronouncing upon botanical matters.

name: Roofer
description: <name> felt that [his/her] dizzying head for heights was a divine gift, to be used in architectural celebration of Our Lord. Working among the angels on the great spire of Salisbury Cathedral was the pinnacle of [his/her] career.

name: Bowyer
description: It was said that <name> annihilated 23 French warriors at L’Ecluse, each dispatched with a single, mercifully accurate shot. [His/Her] fame as an archer was only surpassed by <name>’s skill with yew, building fine longbows. They were greatly prized.

name: Carpenter
description: <name> was a member of the Brotherhood of Carpenters, a guild that offered heavenly rewards. To work all day with wood, knowing that in death the Brotherhood would pay for burial and even have prayers said at the chantry made <name> deeply thankful.

name: Wheelwright
description: <name> of <origin> believed there were many spokes in the wheel of life. [He/She] enjoyed lending a hand with repairs and building projects, even fashioning a crucifix at the behest of a group of mummers for their mystery play.

name: Builder
description: From sawn timber lintel frames to trampled cob for thick, curved walls, <name> could work them with [his/her] strong, raw hands. <name> was known to be rough and ready, just as quick to anger as to lauch into bawdy tales or raucous songs.

name: Brick maker
description: <name> loved the slippery feeling of earth between [his/her] toes. [He/She] spent a happy childhood plugging weathered clay in the yards of Hull, forming an array of ruddy blocks destined for castles and fortresses. [He/She] was an absolute brick.

name: Shipwright
description: <name> had done [his/her] time building vessels on the docks, and could turn [his/her] calloused hand to all manner of construction. Ports being rough and ready places, <name> also knew how to throw a punch and dodge a scoundrel's shiv.

name: Innkeep
description: <name> was known for the crustiest pie pastry in <origin>, and poured a generous pitcher of ale to boot. Jovial and fair, [he/she] never hesitated to knock a few thick heads together if fights broke out, either.

name: Butcher
description: <name> knew animals inside out, as befits a member of the Butcher's Guild. [He/She] had a gentle way with all beasts, and dealt their fate swiftly. <name> knows how to prepare exotic cuts fit for a king, which peasants have never tasted.

name: Chef
description: Once an enfant de cuisine under the great master Taillevent, <name> became chef to the great houses of England. Despite [his/her] snobbery, there's no denying <name>'s culinary expertise regarding all manner of edible flora, fauna, and fungi.

name: Brewster
description: You could tell <name>'s profession by [his/her] tall black hat and broomstick. Yes, [he/she] brewed ale. <name> was a grafter, and resented the Abbot's assumption that [he/she] used [his/her] wiles to get pious men drunk. You can't hold back an entrepreneur.

name: Architect
description: If truth be told, <name> was jealous of Henry Yeverley. Although [he/she] could never rival the Master Mason of the King's Works, <name> thought [his/her] advanced ideas on architecture, acquired at the Château de Vincennes, worthy of greater renown.

name: Master builder
description: <name> loved getting stuck into a complex project. [He/She] spent many years crossing Europe in search of instruction. <name> understood how to create gravity-defying structures with stone and iron, taught by the nameless, genius cathedral builders.

name: Engineer
description: <name> took pride in the vast engines of war [he/she] designed. <name> dreamed of one day creating a device as legendary as the great Warwolf trebuchet created by Master James of St. George. How the tarbarrels and corpses would fly!

name: Scribe
description: The pen is mightier than the sword, and <name> had certainly reveled in a little power. Called upon to wield [his/her] quill by merchants and gentry, <name> recorded their contracts, their laws and their deaths in littera antiqua, with a flourish.

name: Monk
description: <name> liked to potter in the still room, with [his/her] salves and potions. Those brought to the hospital were truly at the mercy of God. But <name> liked to offer what little curative help [he/she] could to ease their suffering.

name: Hunter
description: They said in <origin> that <name> was born with a bow in [his/her] hand. In the warmer months, <name> would hunt wolves, [his/her] tongue lolling and eyes bright as [he/she] loped through the forest, lithe, invisible, and poised to strike.

name: Archer
description: From being fostered as a squire through to becoming a mounted archer, <name> was a true career soldier. Scarred and surly, [he/she] had kept a cool head at Saint-Omer and Morlaix, escaping without victory but with [his/her] life.

name: Recruit
description: <name> practiced when [he/she] could with the longbow, but ploughing and reaping duties generally took precedence. No matter, <name> was enlisted to fight in France, ending at the Siege of Tournai. A string to [his/her] bow and a tale for the fireside.

name: Healer
description: A cloistered life, tending the abbey gardens and copying fine manuscripts, spun <name> along a golden thread of erudition. Alas, the pitiless Abbott urged [him/her] to go forth and heal the sick and the poor. So, reluctantly, <name>’s exile began.

name: Field doctor
description: By day, <name> tended fallen troops. But at night, the rank threat of battlefield dysentery and marsh fever invaded [his/her] sleep. Bad air from bloated corpses was the stuff of nightmares. Of the four horsemen, <name> dreaded pestilence most.

name: Nun
description: <name>'s family paid the church her dowry, granting her a pious and cloistered life. Instead, a small, persistent voice bid her roam over battlefields, stitching up wounds and praying with the broken as they gasped their last. It was <name>'s calling.

name: Knight
description: Chivalry was <name>'s lifeblood, and [he/she] would die for honour. A knight of St John, <name> had become a warrior monk, defended Rhodes from infidels. Loyalty, justice and generosity were [his/her] watchwords, but woe betide the summa culpabilis.

name: Soldier
description: <name> had seen gruesome battles, weak leaders and fearsome foes. Expecting to face death in France, <name> trained constantly and was fighting fit, belligerent and always guarded. We often give our enemies the means of our own destruction.

name: Army cook
description: An army marches on its stomach, and <name> knew how to keep the campfires burning and soldier's bellies full. [His/Her] meals weren't exactly gourmet but <name> was a keen butcher, and could fillet the opposition pretty skillfuly in retreat.

name: Mercenary
description: <name> had roamed Italy causing the worst kinds of trouble with the Company of St George, a group of freemen whose goal was pillaging and chaos. All good things must end, and <name> had subsequently dug ditches and escaped hanging for petty thievery.

name: Farrier
description: <name> is a horse whisperer. [He/She] keeps equine hooves healthy and shod in iron. It doesn't pay much, but it's a stable job.

name: Lorimer
description: <name> has furrows of concentration etched on [his/her] brow, and brawny arms from working hammer and bellows. Whether a humble horse bit or a knight's spurs, <name> could craft them.

name: Blacksmith
description: Broad and taciturn, <name> believed [his/her] art helped forge Anglalonde, aided by the gods. 'Weland gave the Sword, The Sword gave the Treasure, and the Treasure gave the Law,' so it was said. And <name> repeated that often, to any who listened.

name: Armourer
description: <name> could bend anything to [his/her] will, especially bright metal. Formerly apprentice to a master from Chartres, <name>'s hammer and nimble fingers had worked long years in the armouries of the London arsenal. [He/She] had saved countless lives.

name: Arrowsmith
description: Tipped with blade or barbed, <name> had been turning out arrow heads since [he/she] was 14. [He/She] sometimes wondered how many of [his/her] creations had found their mark, staining the ruddy battlefields of Sluys and Crecy.

name: Barber
description: Need a close shave? When it was time to remove a troublesome beard or festering limb, <name> would merrily oblige. [He/She] loved to gossip almost as much as letting blood. <name> was often the first to know, and, for many, the last they would see.

name: Courtesan
description: <name> speaks soft and low, with a gentle laugh as pleasing as birdsong. Despite being a great storyteller, nobody knows [his/her] chequered history at court. However, <name> knows a tasty little secret about almost everyone else...

name: Alchemist
description: <name> had become disillusioned questing for the Philosopher's Stone, and sought the Elixir of Youth. [He/She] could read Greek and Arabic and made copious notes in code. <name> occasionally despaired, [his/her] dreams reduced to glittering dross.

name: Peddler
description: Traveller <name> carried needful supplies on [his/her] back like a snail, toiling between remote hamlets. The insular indwellers were always suspicious. Each time, <name> sweet-talked them into trusting [him/her], so that the bargaining could begin.

name: Tanner
description: <name> knew how to tan a hide with an animal's own brains, and with the alchemy of wood ash, excrement and festering bark. Without <name>, no one would have shoes, armour or saddles. But [he/she] was hardly popular. As jobs go, <name>'s really stank.

name: Cordwainer
description: <name> entered the Cordwainers' Guild by patrimony - 'Corio et Arte' had been [his/her] father's favourite refrain. The scent of leather revived unbidden memories of London ateliers in the shadow of St Paul's, bustling with shoemakers like <name>.

name: Journeyman armourer
description: <name> began with cuir bouilli, leather boiled in wax and sturdy enough to give a commoner some battlefield protection. Later [he/she] progressed to Brigandine armour, riveting on metal plate to shield the heart. <name> was also serviceable with a bow.

name: Cobbler
description: Hailing from <origin>, <name> liked to roam up over the downs and through the ferny holloways of England. Villagers always welcomed [him/her], as even the most humble carl or cotter had shoes for <name> to mend.

name: Miner
description: <name> had done [his/her] time in the Low Peak lead fields and the Welsh mines of the Black Prince. Pale and shunning daylight like many miners, <name> had hollow eyes and headaches. Glistening veins of gold caressed [his/her] dreams.

name: Franklin
description: Tilling lynchets into the poor, hilly soil near <origin> had been a last resort as fertile land was scarce. But <name> had done well, and won the freedom to farm their own hide. <name> felt pride, but mainly relief. [He/She] soldiered on.

name: Carter
description: <name> got sick of shoveling dung with the reeve looking over [his/her] shoulder. And sicker still of the miserable husbandman who didn't pay fair and square in ale when <name> unloaded it onto the fields. At least [he/she] had a strong back.

name: Grave digger
description: <name> dug the graves at <origin> churchyard. But it was on the bloodied field at Crécy that [he/she] did [his/her] finest work. To crack French skulls in a ditch hewn with the very same pickaxe gave <name> endless satisfaction.

name: Berner
description: <name> was top dog, the leader of the pack. [He/She] cared for the hounds, and in return these dogs were fiercely loyal. Although not of high rank, <name> commanded respect. Hounds can be ferocious when crossed.

name: Turnkey
description: Feeding, cleaning, interrogating. <name> liked the weight of keys swaying on [his/her] belt and the smell of damp straw. [He/She] was ambitious, some might say authoritarian.

name: Netmaker
description: <name> tied fragile prayers into knots of hempen twine with calloused hands. [He/She] never failed to wet the nets with a libation, in hopes of a hefty catch.

name: Recuperant
description: <name> learned patience by stitching wounds and waiting for health to return in the infirmary. [He/She] nursed a quiet resilience noticed by few.

name: Squire
description: <name> polished arms humbly, and dreamed of carrying a banner. [He/She] knew how to clean blades, take bruises, and rise early.

name: Fen scout
description: <name> knew where river mud sucked and where raiders struck. [His/Her] wyrd was written in silt and sedge.

name: Nitre miner
description: <name> made ends meet by scraping crusted saltpetre from the walls of the grotto that also served as [his/her] home. The coughing and headaches seemed a fair price to pay.

name: Quacksalver
description: <name> healed with trickery and makeshift prayer, and sometimes - just sometimes - a steady hand.

name: Brawler
description: Where laws fail, fists rule. <name> had earned coin and broken teeth brawling for bed, board and booze.

name: Infirmarian
description: <name> spent years tending the broken; scrubbing bloody flagstones, wiping seeping wounds. Neither soldier, nor sage - just a steady hand when it mattered most.

name: Quartermaster
description: <name> knew the importance of maintaining supplies since the campaign against the Scots at Neville's Cross. [He/She] could dress a wound, clothe a man, or bargain for a bucket, but had never fired a single arrow.

name: Delver
description: <name> hated the serf's life. [He/She] preferred to vanish into rock or river, emerging hours later with raw ore gleaming and the perfect story to tell.

name: Marksage
description: <name>'s bow was a puzzle, not a weapon. [He/She] sensed windrift and the curve of distance, seeing angles comrades missed. [He/She] had become a legend among archers who saw action at Calais.

name: Hermit
description: <name> had inadvertently gone from beggar to hermit, when voices [he/she] heard were deemed holy. Solitary life and food offerings from locals were both greatly beneficial in finding peace of mind.

name: Tutor
description: If <name> could instil [his/her] love of learning in [his/her] small students, it would be a reward in itself. Sadly the young Lordships were spoiled brats, who showed little promise.

name: Bear baiter
description: <name> had to keep the bear in fine fettle, but the dogs were replaceable. [He/She] stayed in the shadows and let the fur fly, once the wagers had been made.
